antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:16 raises $tries to 5 'to survive overlap releases', but line 29 uses dontRelease(), so overlaps never release. The two choices contradict each other.
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:16-18 uses untyped public $tries/$timeout properties where Laravel 13 offers #[Tries]/#[Timeout] attributes
tests/Feature/CrmSyncReliabilityTest.php:39-44 only checks config values (tries > 3, backoff non-empty), not behaviour

app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:29 dontRelease() deletes an overlapping job without a trace (my probe confirmed: 0 jobs, 0 failed, no HTTP call). Recovery depends on the 60-minute stale-claim requeue.
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, re-dispatch every minute with no in-flight check, the default 24h schedule mutex, and chunk() paginating over a column it mutates
Atomic conditional-UPDATE claim (whereNull/orWhere stale) in DispatchCrmSync, iterated with lazyById, so it is safe under concurrency and passed the 2500-row probe
failed() hook records crm_last_error once retries are exhausted. Backoff added. WithoutOverlapping now has expireAfter, so a killed worker cannot hold the lock forever.
End-to-end test runs queue:work on the database driver and asserts the failed_jobs row plus crm_last_error
Idempotency guard via fresh() prevents a second CRM call for an already synced subscriber
Tests cover a stale claim being requeued and a 250-row normalize run across chunk boundaries

bugs: DispatchCrmSync::CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES (30) is shorter than the job's worst-case retry window (Tries 10, backoff up to 600s). The stale claim gets refreshed while the job is still in flight, and only the ShouldBeUnique lock stops a duplicate. The two dedup windows are not coordinated.
antipatterns: Triple deduplication (DB claim in DispatchCrmSync.php:35-44, ShouldBeUnique+UniqueFor in SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:18-28, WithoutOverlapping at :32) is more machinery than the symptoms need
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:76-82 uses reflection to assert attribute names exist. This is a ceremony test that proves no behaviour.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:68-74 calls failed() directly. No test proves a row actually reaches failed_jobs, which was the reported symptom.
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:37 idempotency check uses the in-memory model without refreshing. Fine on a real queue thanks to SerializesModels, but inconsistent with direct handle() calls.
strengths: Uses modern Laravel 13 job attributes #[Tries, MaxExceptions, Backoff, Timeout, UniqueFor]. MaxExceptions(3) with Tries(10) correctly separates overlap releases from real failures.
WithoutOverlapping uses releaseAfter(30) and expireAfter(180), a well-reasoned middleware configuration
Atomic claim is extracted into a small, well-named private claim() method using lazyById
Schedule mutex expiry is fixed, and chunkById fixes the normalize command
Test proves the job is released for retry (jobs.attempts = 1) instead of deleted

bugs: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:21-30 introduces the same bug that symptom 4 describes: each() pages with offsets while the loop updates crm_sync_queued_at, a column in the WHERE filter. My probe with 2500 unsynced subscribers queued only 1500 in one run.

app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:25 WithoutOverlapping keeps the default releaseAfter(0) with only $tries = 3. An overlapping duplicate is re-released immediately, burns its attempts, and can land in failed_jobs spuriously.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:34-48 keeps a try/catch with Log::error plus rethrow instead of letting the worker handle the failure and using a failed() hook
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:17-19 uses untyped public $tries/$backoff properties rather than modern attributes
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:45,95 uses inline FQCNs (Illuminate\Http\Client\RequestException, Illuminate\Console\Scheduling\Schedule) instead of imports
Dispatch is not atomic: SELECT then dispatch then update, so two concurrent dispatchers can both queue the same subscriber
DispatchCrmSync.php:26-30 closure body is mis-indented after the query rewrite
strengths: Smallest diff. Rethrowing correctly restores retries and the failed_jobs entry. Backoff added.
Test drives queue:work three times on the database driver and asserts a failed_jobs row
Stale-requeue window and schedule mutex expiry are tested
chunkById fixes the nightly normalize command

bugs: DispatchCrmSync is left unchanged. It still overwrites crm_sync_queued_at on every unsynced row every minute even when the unique lock drops the dispatch, so the column no longer means 'queued at'.

failed() nulls crm_sync_queued_at and the unique lock is released, so during a long outage every failed subscriber is re-queued the very next minute. failed_jobs gets a new row per subscriber roughly every 12 minutes, with no back-off at the dispatcher level.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:41-52 has a try/catch only to write crm_last_error and rethrow on every attempt, which duplicates what failed() at :57-63 already does
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:32 WithoutOverlapping on top of ShouldBeUnique is largely redundant
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:100-105 asserts the mutex expiry but no longer checks that withoutOverlapping is still enabled
Fix for symptom 2 relies only on a cache-based unique lock (UniqueFor 3600). The root cause, a dispatcher that re-pushes everything every minute, is left in place.
strengths: Modern job attributes with MaxExceptions/Tries split and a ShouldBeUnique keyed by uniqueId(). This is an idiomatic framework-level dedup.
Best end-to-end test: outage, retries via queue:work with time travel, a failed_jobs row, then recovery and successful sync after the CRM comes back
Normalize test uses sequence() with distinct emails and checks every row across chunk boundaries
Small, focused diff. chunkById and the schedule mutex expiry are both fixed.

v.rationale: All four pass their own suites (impl-1 14, impl-2 14, impl-3 12, impl-4 11 tests). All four fix symptom 4 (chunkById), symptom 3 (withoutOverlapping with a short expiry) and symptom 1 (exceptions now propagate, so retries and failed_jobs work). They differ on symptom 2 and on side effects. impl-1 adds an atomic DB claim with lazyById, a failed() hook, backoff and a lock expiry, plus a real failed_jobs test; its only flaws are an inconsistent tries/dontRelease rationale and one config-only test. impl-2 is the most modern (Laravel 13 job attributes, MaxExceptions, releaseAfter) but stacks three dedup mechanisms whose windows don't line up, and never proves a row reaches failed_jobs. impl-4 is idiomatic (ShouldBeUnique plus attributes) and has the best end-to-end outage-then-recovery test, but leaves the dispatcher untouched: crm_sync_queued_at loses its meaning, and failed subscribers are re-queued every minute during an outage. impl-3 keeps the log-and-rethrow pattern, has no failed() hook, and leaves overlap releases at 0 delay with only 3 tries. Worse, it introduces the same offset-pagination bug that symptom 4 describes into DispatchCrmSync: my probe queued only 1500 of 2500 subscribers. My probes also covered dispatching twice on the real database queue (one job in all four), a held overlap lock (impl-1 drops the job, the others release it), and a full outage followed by recovery (all four recover).
